rounds.text: Mercury EV-Tech Ltd presents a significant valuation disconnect, trading at a P/E of 135x compared to a sector benchmark of just 23.48x [E1, E6]. This premium is difficult to justify given that the company’s return on equity of 1.56% and return on capital employed of 2.46% significantly underperform their respective sector benchmarks of 11.88% and 12.89% [E9, E10]. The company is currently burning cash, evidenced by negative operating cash flow of Rs -32 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -55 Cr in March 2026 [E30, E31]. Furthermore, the stock’s recent performance is concerning, with compounded sales growth of -11% and profit growth of -50% over the trailing twelve months [E15, E17]. A discounted cash flow analysis suggests an intrinsic value of Rs 9 per share, implying a margin of safety of -264.4% [E39, E40]. Conceded: the company maintains a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.16x and has demonstrated a 3-year compounded sales growth of 85% [E14, E32]. Despite these historical figures, the current price implies an unrealistic 36.4% earnings growth rate, which is disconnected from the company's recent operational deceleration [E41, E63].
